summary: Phase F10.2 cod_payment mismatch fix RE-VERIFIED. All 5/5 tests now pass (previously 4/5 in iteration 52). The previously-failing scenario — GET /api/shipments/{id} after a discrepant cod_payment import surfacing `import_validation_alerts` — now works correctly. Confirmed the alert-projection block was added inside the `if import_type == 'cod_payment':` branch at /app/backend/routers/shipment_import.py:1213-1231, guarded by `if mismatches:` so exact matches produce no alert. Discrepant upload (cod_collected=719 vs cod_amount=669 on EG350860354IN) now stamps `import_validation_alerts=[{field:'cod_amount', existing:669, imported:719, at:<iso>}]` on the shipment doc. Regression tests (baseline correction, batch tally mismatch registration, exact-match clean, booking match, booking diverge) all continue to pass.

minor.issue: Same projection gap likely still exists for delivery imports — cross-verify mismatches populate the batch but may not reach `shipment.import_validation_alerts`. Not in scope for F10.2 but worth unifying the alert-stamping into a shared post-loop block.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correctly scoped: the projection block sits inside the `if import_type == 'cod_payment':` branch (shipment_import.py:1213-1231), guarded by `if mismatches:`, so clean matches leave the field untouched (verified by test_cod_payment_matching_upload_no_mismatch).

Alert projection overwrites (not appends to) `import_validation_alerts` — this is called out in the code comment (line 1219-1221) and is by-design: newest run wins. That matches the booking branch behaviour.
shipment_import.py is now 1451 lines — still above the 700-line guideline. Consider extracting per-import-type post-processing into helper modules to improve maintainability. Non-blocking.
seed_data_creation: None. Reused existing shipment EG350860354IN (amount=719, cod_amount=669) from admin@test.com account.
context_for_next_testing_agent: F10.2 cod_payment mismatch flow is fully verified. If future changes touch shipment_import.py's commit endpoint, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_phase_f10_2_cod_payment_mismatch.py. Delivery-import branch was flagged as a similar-gap candidate in iteration 52 but is out of scope for F10.2.
rca_of_issue: Iteration 52 identified that the cod_payment branch of the /api/shipments/import/commit endpoint detected mismatches correctly (batch row flagged matched_mismatch with a `cod_amount` entry) but never projected them onto `shipment.import_validation_alerts`, so the Shipment Details 'Payment discrepancy' alert stayed silent. Fix applied at shipment_import.py:1213-1231 mirrors the booking-branch stamping (lines 1134-1142) inside the cod_payment branch, guarded by `if mismatches:` for safety on exact-match remits. Verified in iteration 53 by test_shipment_details_surfaces_import_alert which now passes.
